concerns.text: Consumer-before-producer at the semantic level: T005 sweeps N ∈ {100,500,1000,2000} × seeds {42,123,456,789} 'consuming checksummed raw matrices', but the only raw matrix any task produces or references is data/raw/matrix_N1000_seed42.npy (T003). No task generates or checksums the other 15 N/seed combinations, so T005's declared inputs do not exist at execution time. Add a producer task (or extend T005 to generate them) before the sweep.

T010 consumes 'data/configs/density_grid.json' via '--grid-file', but no task in this document produces that grid file (T005's grid is defined inline). A consumer task whose input artifact has no producer violates producer-before-consumer; either add a task that writes density_grid.json with its contents specified, or inline the grid definition in T010 as T005 does.

The 'Execution order' section states 'T004 and T005 may proceed in parallel after T003', but T004 modifies code/analysis/simulation_loop.py and code/main.py while T005's orchestrator consumes run_single_simulation from that same module. This is a hidden shared-state ordering between the two tasks; either sequence T004 before T005 or state that T005 uses the pre-T004 interface (the sweep does not need T004's serialization changes).
